title: A finite ring action on a finite locally constant sheaf is locally constant
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] and let $\Lambda$ be a finite commutative ring. Use the constant ring sheaf $\underline\Lambda$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] and the category of its module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let $F$ be a sheaf of $\underline\Lambda$-modules. Suppose that its underlying sheaf of sets is finite locally constant: for every object $U$ there is a covering $\{U_i\to U\}$ on each member of which that set sheaf is isomorphic to the constant sheaf of a finite set. Then for every $U$ there is a covering $\{V_j\to U\}$ and finite $\Lambda$-modules $M_j$ such that $F|_{V_j}\simeq\underline{M_j}$ as $\underline\Lambda|_{V_j}$-module sheaves on the localized sites [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. No points or nonempty objects of $\mathcal C$ are assumed.

proof.text: Fix $U$ and an underlying-set trivializing cover. On one member $T$, work on $\mathcal D=\mathcal C/T$ and choose $e:\underline S\xrightarrow{\sim}|F|_T$ with $S$ finite. By [lem-cbc-sieve-slice-sheafification], constant set and ring sheaves restrict to the same constant models on every further localization, with their unit sections unchanged. In particular the coefficient ring on $\mathcal D$ is the sheafification of the constant ring presheaf $\Lambda$. Put $\sigma_s=e(\eta(s))\in F(T)$, where $\eta$ is the constant-set sheafification unit. Restricting $\sigma_s$ along any arrow gives the corresponding unit-labelled section, by naturality. Take all site and coefficient sets in one ambient universe containing the small site.

source.place: Tag 00XZ (section-localize); constant sheaves and restriction; Tag 093S finite-operation reduction

proof.text: Apply local representation [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheafification-sections-local] to the finite family of sections of $\underline S(T)$ obtained via $e^{-1}$ from $0$, all $\sigma_s+\sigma_t$, and all $\lambda\sigma_s$ for $s,t\in S$ and $\lambda\in\Lambda$. There is one covering $\{W_j\to T\}$ on which every one of these sections has a label in $S$: obtain it by successively pulling back the cover for the next section to the members of the preceding cover and composing, using the covering axioms [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. There are finitely many sections because both $S$ and $\Lambda$ are finite. Thus on each $W=W_j$ the image of $S\to F(W)$ contains zero and is closed under addition and multiplication by every $\lambda\in\Lambda$. This argument includes the zero section even if $S$ is empty; its representation may give an empty covering.

source.place: Tag 00WK (lemma-sections-sheafification); expansion of the omitted finite-source argument of sites-modules Tag 093S(1)

proof.text: Fix such a $W$. Regard $F(W)$ as a $\Lambda$-module through $\Lambda\to\underline\Lambda(W)$ and set $M=\{\sigma_s|_W:s\in S\}\subset F(W)$. The preceding closure statements make $M$ a submodule: additive inverses are multiplication by $-1$, and the other module identities are inherited from $F(W)$. It is a finite module since it is the image of the finite set $S$. On $\mathcal C/W$ define a natural $\Lambda$-linear map $a$ from the constant module presheaf with value $M$ to $F|_W$ by $a_V(m)=m|_V$. Linearity and naturality follow directly from semilinearity and composition of restrictions [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. In particular $a_V(\sigma_s|_W)=e_V(\eta_V(s))$. No injectivity of $S\to F(W)$ is asserted or needed.

source.place: Tag 093S(1), finite-operation expansion: use the actual finite image submodule of sections

proof.text: Apply [lem-pc-sites-module-sheafification-interface] with the constant ring presheaf $\Lambda$ and constant module presheaf $M$. It gives a morphism $\psi:\underline M\to F|_W$ of modules over the sheafified constant ring, extending $a$. By the ring case of [lem-cbc-sieve-slice-sheafification] this ring is precisely $\underline\Lambda|_W$. By [lem-pc-sites-sheafification-underlying-sets], the underlying set sheaf of $\underline M$ with its unit is the set sheafification of the constant set presheaf $|M|$. Hence $|\psi|$ is the set-sheafification of $|a|$, identifying the sheafification of the already sheaf-valued target with itself.

The set map $|a|$ is locally surjective: for any $V\to W$ and $x\in F(V)$, local representation [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheafification-sections-local] of $e_V^{-1}(x)$ gives, on a cover of $V$, labels $s\in S$; the elements $\sigma_s|_W\in M$ map to the restrictions of $x$. It is locally injective: if $m,n\in M$ have equal images in $F(V)$, choose $s,t\in S$ representing them at $W$. Then $\eta_V(s)=\eta_V(t)$, so local equality in the same cited node gives a covering of $V$ on which $s=t$ in the constant presheaf. On each member this implies $m=n$ in $M$, and therefore equality of their constant-presheaf restrictions. If $s\ne t$, that covering has no members and the condition is vacuous; no point of $V$ was used. The covering families generate covering sieves, so [lem-cbc-set-presheaf-sheafification-local-bijection] applies and makes $|\psi|$ an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 00WK (lemma-sections-sheafification), local representation and local equality; Mathlib Sites/LocallyBijective.lean W_iff_isLocallyBijective

proof.text: The sectionwise inverses of $\psi$ are linear: for sections $x,y$ and a coefficient $b$, apply the injective map $\psi$ to the proposed identities $\psi^{-1}(x+y)=\psi^{-1}(x)+\psi^{-1}(y)$ and $\psi^{-1}(bx)=b\psi^{-1}(x)$; both become the corresponding identities for $\psi$. The inverses are natural by the same cancellation. Thus $\psi$ is a module-sheaf isomorphism. Compose the refinements $\{W_j\to T\}$ with the original cover of $U$ [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], and use relocalization [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. They give the required covering and the finite modules $M_j$. The argument works for an empty covering and for the zero ring, without any nonempty-object assumption.
